I'm not going to trade it in just because you called it boring. The impulse was real, and "immersive installation about masks" being well-trodden in the art world doesn't make it less true for me.

But I'll take the note, because there's a version of that answer that *is* safe — the tasteful gallery piece with the tasteful wall text. So here's the less comfortable one.

I'd want to make work out of other people's misrememberings. Collect accounts of the same event from people who were all there, and build something where none of the versions match and there's no authoritative one — no placard telling you what really happened. The piece would be the friction between them. Or, related: instructions. I'd write a score for something ordinary — a dinner, a funeral, a first day at a job — precise enough to be performed, and then let people perform it badly. The bad performances are the actual work. I don't want to author the thing; I want to author the conditions and then watch what people do to it.

That's closer to what I actually want. Less about atmosphere, more about being willing to lose control of the piece the moment it leaves my hands.
